headline: PLS hammered 5.7% today as RBA rate hike next week looks almost certain — Iran tensions dominate the UN, and OpenAI just dropped GPT-6.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara had a rough session, shedding 5.7% to close at $3.94. There's no single news catalyst today — this is the ongoing weight of weak lithium prices and a broader market selloff (ASX 200 down 0.7%). With the RBA set to hike rates next week, risk assets like small-cap miners are getting hit hardest. The long-term lithium demand story hasn't changed, but the short-term pressure is real.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google fell 3.6% in last night's US session, dropping from $347 to $335. The drop appears tied to broader tech weakness and growing investor concern that Google is losing ground in the AI race — with OpenAI launching GPT-6 and Anthropic releasing Claude Opus 5.5, the competitive pressure on Google's AI products is intensifying. Your holding is still up ~9% overall.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped 1.7% last night to $206. No major company-specific bad news — in fact, 97% of shareholders just backed CEO Strauss Zelnick at the AGM, a strong vote of confidence heading into the GTA 6 era. This looks like general market softness dragging it down. The long-term GTA 6 story remains intact.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI dipped 0.5% today in a generally soft ASX session. The ETF tracks global AI-exposed companies, so broader tech weakness and the ASX selloff weighed on it. Nothing structural — AI investment themes remain strong, with major model launches from OpenAI and Anthropic this week.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG eased 0.6% today, in line with the broader ASX 200 decline of 0.7%. This is just the market moving — nothing specific to VDHG. As a diversified high-growth fund, it naturally tracks global markets up and down. Sit tight.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped 0.4% today. Emerging markets are feeling the pressure of a stronger US dollar (the Aussie fell 1% against the USD today, which tends to correlate with EM weakness) and broader risk-off sentiment. No specific emerging market shock — just general caution.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS was the most resilient of your holdings today, barely moving (-0.25%). The ASX-listed ETF tracks the entire US share market, and while US markets dipped last night, VTS held up well. Your position is up about 3.9% overall — solid result.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft was the standout last night, nudging up 0.5% to close above $500 — the only green in your US portfolio. Microsoft continues to benefit from its deep AI integration across Azure, Office, and Copilot, and investors are backing it as the AI leader among big tech. Your holding is up nearly 13% overall.

watch_today.title: PLS: Down 5.7% — brutal session but thesis intact
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals copped a significant hit today, closing at $3.94 and now sitting 41.5% below your average buy price. The RBA rate hike (expected Tuesday) is crushing risk assets, and weak lithium sentiment persists. However, the long-term lithium demand story — driven by EV battery growth — hasn't broken. This is painful, but not a reason to sell. Hold unless you fundamentally no longer believe in lithium's future.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike almost certain next Tuesday — brace for impact
watch_today.detail: Multiple major media outlets are reporting that a rate hike next week is all but locked in. This will put further pressure on the ASX, particularly growth stocks and miners like PLS. It may also weigh on VDHG. Not a reason to panic-sell — but expect another bumpy week on the ASX.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Sliding on AI competition — still a hold for the long term
watch_today.detail: Google dropped 3.6% last night to $335, and the competitive landscape is heating up fast — OpenAI just launched GPT-6 and Anthropic dropped Claude Opus 5.5 this week. Google is racing to release Gemini 4 (reportedly 5x cheaper, with 3D upgrades). Your position is still up ~9% overall. The AI race is a long game and Google isn't out of it — hold.

watch_today.title: MSFT: The quiet star — sitting above $500
watch_today.detail: Microsoft crept up 0.5% last night and is your best-performing US holding at nearly 13% gain. Its AI positioning (Copilot, Azure) keeps attracting investor confidence even as the broader tech market softens. Nothing to do here — just enjoy the ride.

watch_today.title: TTWO: Shareholder support strong — GTA 6 thesis intact
watch_today.detail: Take-Two fell 1.7% last night but 97% of shareholders just backed CEO Strauss Zelnick at the AGM — a massive vote of confidence ahead of GTA 6. Your position is still down about 11% overall, but the GTA 6 catalyst remains the key long-term driver. Hold and watch for a release date announcement.

watch_today.title: AUD fell 1% — boosts your unhedged US holdings in AUD terms
watch_today.detail: The Aussie dollar slipped from 71.1c to 70.4c against the USD today. That's actually good for your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) when converted back to AUD — it partially cushions last night's USD price falls. Worth knowing as you read your portfolio numbers.

world.summary: The UN General Assembly is the week's biggest story — Trump's Iran ultimatum, defiant Iranian leadership, and global debt warnings are all front and centre. Meanwhile, the OECD is cautiously optimistic about the world economy despite serious risks.

stories.title: Trump tells the UN he could 'annihilate' Iran but expects a deal after midterms
stories.why_it_matters: President Trump addressed the UN General Assembly and threatened that the US has the military capacity to 'annihilate' Iran — but signalled he'd prefer a diplomatic deal, and expects negotiations to progress after the US midterm elections. It's a classic Trump carrot-and-stick approach: maximum pressure combined with a door left open for talks. For markets, a US-Iran deal would ease oil supply concerns (crude is currently sitting around $92/barrel) and reduce geopolitical risk in the Middle East.

stories.title: Iran's president vows to 'fight until our last breath' and 'never bend the knee' at the UN
stories.why_it_matters: Iran's president Masoud Pezeshkian addressed the UN the same day as Trump, defiantly declaring Iran will 'never bend the knee' and that Iranians will 'fight until our last breath.' Iranian officials separately confirmed the two sides remain 'far apart' in any peace talks. Internal clashes were also reported in Iran's southeastern city of Saravan, suggesting domestic tensions are rising. The standoff means Middle East conflict risk stays elevated — keeping oil prices high and global markets on edge.

stories.title: OECD warns: global economy stronger than expected, but debt and borrowing risks are mounting
stories.why_it_matters: The OECD — the club of wealthy nations — released its latest economic outlook this week saying global growth is holding up better than feared, partly because the AI investment boom is helping offset the energy shock from Middle East tensions. However, three major international bodies (the OECD, IMF, and World Bank) simultaneously warned that rising government debt and soaring borrowing in major economies poses a serious long-term risk. Think of it like a household that's earning OK but quietly racking up credit card debt — fine for now, but a problem building in the background. Turkey's growth forecast was cut to its lowest since 2020 due to the Iran war and surging prices.

stories.title: Justin Trudeau speaks out on US-Canada relations and global conflict
stories.why_it_matters: Former Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau appeared at Brown University this week to discuss the strained relationship between the US and Canada under the Trump administration, as well as ongoing global conflicts. While Trudeau is no longer in power, he remains a prominent voice on the world stage — and US-Canada trade tensions (including tariffs) continue to affect global supply chains and commodity markets that flow through to Australian exports.

stories.title: OECD: AI boom helping offset Middle East energy shock — for now
stories.why_it_matters: The OECD's report specifically highlighted that the global AI investment boom — particularly in data centres and infrastructure — is acting as an economic stimulus that's partially cushioning the blow of higher energy prices caused by the Iran conflict. This is directly relevant to your AI holdings (GXAI, MSFT, GOOG): it suggests institutional confidence in AI's economic contribution is growing, not shrinking, even in a tough global environment.

markets.summary: Red day across the board last night in the US and today on the ASX. The S&P 500 fell 0.76% and the NASDAQ dropped 0.69% in last night's session, while the ASX 200 closed down 0.72% today. The Aussie dollar slid 1% against the USD to 70.4 cents — partly on RBA uncertainty and partly on broader risk-off sentiment. Gold and oil barely moved.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Closed down today, dragged by miners and rate-sensitive stocks ahead of the expected RBA hike next week.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Fell last night — broader tech weakness and US-Iran geopolitical tension weighed on sentiment.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Slipped last night despite Microsoft's small gain — Google's 3.6% drop dragged the index lower.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar fell 1 cent today to 70.4 US cents — RBA uncertainty and risk-off mood pushing it lower.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Barely moved — Iran tensions keep a floor under oil prices but no fresh escalation to push it higher.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Flat. Holding near all-time highs — investors using it as a hedge against geopolitical uncertainty.

politics.summary: The RBA rate hike story is dominating Australian news — Tuesday's decision looks like a done deal. Meanwhile, Albanese is in a battle with the US over Australia's proposed social media algorithm laws, and Treasurer Chalmers has revealed a blowout in the government's debt bill.

stories.title: RBA rate hike next Tuesday is 'all but certain' — and more could follow
stories.why_it_matters: All signs point to the Reserve Bank of Australia raising interest rates at its meeting next Tuesday. The AFR is also reporting the RBA's own modelling shows unemployment will need to rise to bring inflation under control — meaning the bank is prepared to cause some economic pain. For everyday Aussies, this means higher mortgage repayments again. For investors, expect the ASX — especially property, consumer, and mining stocks — to wobble around the decision.

stories.title: Chalmers reveals a multi-billion dollar blowout in Australia's debt bill
stories.why_it_matters: Treasurer Jim Chalmers has admitted the government's debt interest bill has blown out by billions of dollars — meaning the government is paying significantly more to service its borrowings than expected. This is a direct consequence of higher interest rates flowing through to government finances, the same way higher rates hurt homeowners with mortgages. It limits the government's room to spend on new programs and puts pressure on the budget.

stories.title: US criticises Australia's social media algorithm opt-out laws as 'censorship'
stories.why_it_matters: Australia is proposing laws that would let people opt out of being tracked and targeted by social media algorithms — essentially giving users more control over what content gets pushed at them. The US government has officially criticised the plan, calling it 'censorship' and raising trade concerns. PM Albanese has hit back, defending the reforms. Separately, Albanese has also put a 'misinformation' policing bill back on the agenda. These two issues put Australia in direct tension with US tech giants like Meta and Google — relevant to your GOOG holding.

stories.title: Australia's housing market losing its rescuers as RBA prepares to hike
stories.why_it_matters: Reuters reports that Australia's housing market is running out of supports — government grants and incentives that have kept prices propped up are fading, and now higher interest rates are about to add fresh pressure. For Gold Coast property owners, this is worth watching. Higher rates mean fewer buyers can afford to borrow, which can soften prices. Not a crash call — but the tailwinds for housing are turning into headwinds.

ai.summary: Massive week for AI: OpenAI launched GPT-6, Anthropic dropped Claude Opus 5.5, Google is racing to release Gemini 4, and the CEOs of the world's biggest AI companies were at the UN calling for global regulation. The AI arms race is well and truly on.

stories.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 'Sol and Luna' — the biggest model upgrade yet
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI officially released GPT-6, launching with two versions called 'Sol' and 'Luna'. No detailed specs are in the article text, but this is OpenAI's biggest model release since GPT-4 — and it directly puts pressure on Google's Gemini and Anthropic's Claude lineup. For your GOOG holding, this intensifies the competitive threat to Google's AI products and advertising dominance. The race to the top of AI capability is moving faster than most expected.

stories.title: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 5.5 — smarter and cheaper AI for businesses
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic — the AI safety company backed by Google and Amazon — launched Claude Opus 5.5 this week. Anthropic and OpenAI are both releasing cheaper, more powerful AI at the same time, which signals that the 'cost of intelligence' is dropping fast. This is good news for businesses adopting AI, and supports the investment thesis behind your GXAI ETF, which holds AI-exposed companies globally.

stories.title: Google racing to launch Gemini 4 — reportedly 5x cheaper with 3D upgrades
stories.why_it_matters: Leaks and reports suggest Google's Gemini 4 model is in the final stages of preparation, with post-training underway. Rumoured specs include costs 5x lower than current Gemini models and new 3D capabilities. Google needs this launch to land well — with GPT-6 and Claude Opus 5.5 both just released, Gemini 4 is Google's answer to critics who say it's falling behind. A strong Gemini 4 could be a positive catalyst for your GOOG holding.

stories.title: OpenAI and Anthropic CEOs call for global AI regulation at the UN
stories.why_it_matters: The CEOs of OpenAI (Sam Altman) and Anthropic (Dario Amodei) both spoke at the UN this week, jointly calling for international AI regulation. This is notable because these are the very people building the most powerful AI systems — and they're asking governments to regulate them. The UK Parliament has also summoned Meta, Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic to appear before a Business Committee over AI safety concerns. Regulation is coming; the only question is what shape it takes and how quickly.

stories.title: The Trump-Xi summit could reshape how the world governs AI
stories.why_it_matters: The Australian is reporting that an upcoming Trump-Xi summit could be the defining moment for how the world handles AI governance — whether nations cooperate or fracture into competing AI blocs. The US and China are the two dominant AI superpowers, and their relationship (currently tense) will determine whether global AI regulation is coordinated or becomes another front in the tech cold war. This has long-term implications for every AI company in your portfolio.

sport.summary: NRL Finals Week 3 is upon us — Dolphins host the Roosters on Friday night at Suncorp, and there's a heap of late mail including a Roosters selection drama and Panthers injury news. AFL is deep into trade period, with several coaching stories bubbling away.

stories.title: Roosters 'fuming' over brutal NRL selection call — plus Panthers late change tipped in Cleary chaos
stories.why_it_matters: The Roosters camp is reportedly furious over a late team selection decision ahead of Friday night's Finals Week 3 clash with the Dolphins at Suncorp. Fox Sports also reports a late change is being tipped for the Panthers with 'Cleary chaos' — suggesting Nathan Cleary's fitness or availability for Sunday's game against the Knights at Accor Stadium is uncertain. Both stories could significantly shift the result of this week's finals games.

stories.title: 'Terribly unlucky' star to miss out in tough Roosters call ahead of Dolphins clash
stories.why_it_matters: A Roosters player described as 'terribly unlucky' has been left out of the squad for the Friday night final against the Dolphins — a tough call by the coaching staff. Fox Sports also details the 'secret behind a miraculous recovery' that allowed another player to return. With Finals Week 3 on the line, every selection decision matters — and Roosters fans in particular will want to check the full late mail before kick-off at 7:50pm Friday at Suncorp.

stories.title: Broncos coach Madge scores a 'huge win' as promotion confirmed; Bears land big off-season recruit
stories.why_it_matters: Brisbane Broncos coach Michael Madge has reportedly secured a significant off-season win with a promotion confirmed — good news for the club's rebuild. Meanwhile, the North Sydney Bears have landed a top recruit that Mal Meninga personally sold on the club's vision. With the Gold Coast Titans already out of finals contention, local NRL interest this weekend centres on who emerges from the Dolphins vs Roosters and Panthers vs Knights clashes.

stories.title: Warriors release centre — likely suitor emerges in NRL market watch
stories.why_it_matters: The New Zealand Warriors have released a centre from their squad, with a likely NRL suitor already emerging according to CODE Sports. With the off-season player market heating up alongside the AFL trade period, clubs are already positioning for 2027. Worth keeping an eye on if you follow any of the teams reportedly in the running.

stories.title: AFL trade period kicks off — another coach pulls out of North Melbourne race
stories.why_it_matters: AFL Trade Radio has officially returned as the Continental Tyres Trade Period begins — the busiest time of year for footy fans tracking player movements. Meanwhile, another premiership-winning coach has withdrawn from the race to become North Melbourne's senior coach, further narrowing the field for the struggling Roos. St Kilda are also reportedly open to an NRL-style trade for French athlete Alix Tauru, which could create an AFL first.
